panels.title: Spans received /s
panels.description: Spans arriving from the two SGLang workers and the router over OTLP/gRPC :4317.

panels.title: Spans exported /s
panels.description: Spans successfully POSTed to Langfuse /api/public/otel. Should track the receiver rate.

panels.title: Export failures /s
panels.description: Sustained nonzero almost always means LANGFUSE_OTEL_AUTH no longer matches a live project key pair — a 401 that is indistinguishable from a wrong key. See docs/LANGFUSE.md.

panels.title: Refused by memory_limiter /s
panels.description: Backpressure at the front door: the collector hit its 512 MiB soft limit and rejected spans rather than grow. Raise the limit or widen the batch settings.

panels.title: Span throughput — received vs exported vs dropped
panels.description: accepted and sent should sit on top of each other. Any persistent gap is span loss — the pipeline is asynchronous, so nothing upstream will complain about it.

panels.title: Export queue depth vs capacity
panels.description:
The buffer that lets a Langfuse restart cost nothing. Depth climbing toward capacity means Langfuse is not draining and spans are about to be dropped on the floor.

Stale `otlphttp/langfuse` series may linger next to `otlp_http/langfuse`: the exporter was renamed when the old alias started logging a deprecation warning.

panels.title: Queue utilisation
panels.description: Alert threshold is 50% sustained — see prometheus/alerts.yml.

panels.title: Batch send size (p50/p95)
panels.description: Spans per POST. Configured send_batch_size is 512 with a max of 1024. A p95 pinned at 512 means the batcher is filling on size rather than timing out, i.e. the pipeline is busy.

panels.title: Batch flushes by trigger
panels.description: At this node's span rate nearly every flush is a timeout flush, which is the expected shape for low, bursty traffic.

panels.title: Collector CPU
panels.description: Measured at ~0.03% of one core. The trace pipeline is not a meaningful tenant on cores 48-55.

panels.title: Collector memory
panels.description: memory_limiter is set to 512 MiB with a 128 MiB spike allowance; RSS approaching that is what produces the refused spans on the first row.

panels.title: Collector up
panels.description: Stands in for a container healthcheck: the core collector image is distroless, so no CMD-SHELL probe can run in it.

panels.title: Disk used vs total (data disk)
panels.description: Added after an audit found ~1.0 GB of untenanted system log tables plus an 830 MB unrotated server log backing 396 KiB of actual traces. Retention is now bounded by clickhouse/config.d — this panel is how a regression gets noticed before it is measured in gigabytes.

panels.title: MergeTree bytes — total vs system tables
panels.description: The gap between these two lines is the real trace payload. If the system.* line dominates again, ClickHouse has gone back to spending more on self-observation than on data.

panels.title: Active parts / tables
panels.description: A part count climbing without bound means merges are not keeping up.

panels.title: Failed queries /s
panels.description: Langfuse surfaces ingestion errors slowly; this shows them at the database.

title: Trace Pipeline
description: SGLang spans -> OTel Collector -> Langfuse -> ClickHouse. Asynchronous end to end, so failures here are silent: nothing in the request path degrades when traces stop arriving.
